minutes.headline: Sewer Commission lost its quorum to a departing chair and business manager, and approved placeholder FY24 budget-amendment articles.
minutes.summary: At the last meeting before the chair and business manager Paula leave, the commission voted on a volunteer-recruitment mailing, placeholder special town meeting articles, a Mass One suction line repair, line-item transfers and a grease trap fine. Much of the discussion was about how the commission can function with only three members and no quorum. The chair, Paula and the commissioners were thanked at length.

public_comment.topic: The chair asked for public comment and none was offered; commissioners and staff instead praised the departing business manager.
Second call for public comment; none from the public. Commissioners and staff thanked the chair for his service.

votes.motion: Have Mike Mackin write a letter to the editor about filling sewer commission vacancies.
Have the town manager send the volunteer recruitment letter to the roughly 700-plus sewer customers.
Approve submission of placeholder articles to adjust the fiscal 24 sewer budget as needed at year close.
Accept the CTE estimate for repair of the suction lines plus up to an additional amount for pumping.
Authorize Paula to request the proposed budget line-item transfers.
Impose the fine on the one non-compliant grease trap establishment.

budget_items.what_was_said: Mailing to about 751 customers will cost almost the figure stated in postage; the town would not pay so the sewer budget absorbs it.
Budget was set for this fiscal year but the estimate is higher; contractor cost plus pumping, similar to the earlier force main repair.

budget_items.topic: Pumping allowance for the line repair
budget_items.what_was_said: Commissioners discussed capping pumping and settled on a higher cap on staff recommendation. Paula said the project fits within the total existing budget.
Betterment revenue is down; outsourcing/consulting reduced, utilities and office expense increased, connection fees and capital contribution lines raised. Bottom line stays the same.

budget_items.topic: Energy grant for Dana Street project
budget_items.what_was_said: Potential grant funding via the Green Communities committee, pending whether they submit a fall application.
Regulations set the fee, with a separate fine for non-compliance.

budget_items.topic: State revolving fund for capital plan
budget_items.what_was_said: Possible state revolving loan funding for generators and aging system repairs, with a rough minimum project size mentioned.
Paula believes there will be a surplus because properties sold and betterments were paid off, but the year is not closed.

transfers.description: Line-item transfers within the sewer budget (outsourcing, utilities, legal, office, capital, connection fees) were authorized to be requested; specific transfer amounts were not stated.

decisions.decision: Assistant business manager interviews will wait until the new business manager is in place; Mike Mackin will sit in on interviews.
The recruitment letter will go out from the Office of the Town Manager and will add that extensions must be within the sewer service area; postage is absorbed by the sewer budget.
Bill will talk to the town manager and possibly the select board about appointing an interim or former commissioner to restore a quorum.
Upcoming meetings listed for September 10, September 24, October 8 and October 29.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission approved placeholder special town meeting articles so the fiscal 24 sewer budget can be adjusted when the year closes.
Commissioners discussed how to function with only three members and no quorum; the Town Manager and possibly the Select Board will be asked about an interim appointment.
The commission voted to accept an estimate for repairing the Mass One suction lines, plus an allowance for pumping, with the estimate above what was budgeted for the year.
The commission authorized the business manager to request line-item budget transfers, and voted to impose a fine on the one grease trap establishment found non-compliant.
Two votes aimed at filling commission vacancies passed: a letter to the editor, and a recruitment letter to sewer customers sent from the Town Manager's office.

why_it_matters: A sewer commission without a quorum cannot vote on rates, repairs or budget transfers, so sewer service decisions depend on the vacancies being filled.
Sewer customers may be asked to vote on the placeholder articles at a special town meeting, and the repair, mailing and transfers are paid from the sewer budget rather than general tax revenue.
watch_next: Upcoming commission meetings on September 10, September 24, October 8 and October 29.
Whether the Town Manager or Select Board appoints an interim or former commissioner to restore a quorum.
